## Preliminaries

**Working scope (declared as assumption, not fact).** Mic 7:1-20 (minus the by-design gap at v11) is taken as a single reading unit: Micah's own personal lament over total societal breakdown, down to the level of family betrayal (vv1-6); his own pivot to confident trust and genuine confession (vv7-10); a promise of ingathering alongside continued judgment on the wider earth (vv12-13); a prayer for shepherding, answered by a promised new exodus (vv14-15); the nations' own total reversal from hostility to humbled fear (vv16-17); and the book's closing doxology to the LORD's own forgiving, covenant-faithful character (vv18-20). "Bearing on the inner being" includes: (i) Micah himself, in his most sustained first-person presence in the book — lamenting (v1), trusting (v7), confessing (v9), and directly addressing a personified enemy (v8, v10); (ii) the total collapse of ordinary trust, down to the nuclear family itself (vv5-6); (iii) "your people," prayed for as a flock (v14); (iv) "the nations," given the book's most complete reversal, from hostility/mockery to trembling fear (vv16-17); (v) the LORD, closing the book as the one "who pardons iniquity... delights in steadfast love" (vv18-20).

**Reading rule applied.** No [AMBIGUOUS]-span STEP-live resolution was needed — the base extract reports 100% meaning coverage for this range (218/218 non-particle spans). Register: personal lament (vv1-2), extended social-breakdown indictment (vv3-6), a decisive first-person pivot to trust (v7), direct address to a personified enemy (vv8-10), a promise-oracle (vv12-15), narrated reversal (vv16-17), and closing hymnic doxology (vv18-20).

Carried forward: Micah's own first-person lament voice (Mic 1:8, now recurring at v1); the corrupt "prince... judge... great man" charge (Mic 3:1, 9, 11, recurring at v3); the "my people rising up as an enemy" reversal (Mic 2:8, now escalated to full household betrayal at vv5-6); the exodus recital (Mic 6:4, now recurring as a FUTURE promise at v15); the nations' hostile mockery (Mic 4:11, now reversed at vv16-17); "from of old"/ancient covenant language (Mic 5:2, recurring at v20).

## Per-verse debate

### Mic 7:1

> Woe is me! For I have become as when the summer fruit has been gathered, as when the grapes have been gleaned: there is no cluster to eat, no first-ripe fig that my soul desires.

**Observation.** "Woe [H0480] is me! For I have become as when the summer fruit [H7019] has been gathered [H0625], as when the grapes [H1210] have been gleaned [H5955]: there is no [H0369] cluster [H0811] to eat [H0398], no first-ripe fig [H1063] that my soul [H5315L] desires [H0183]."

**Operation 1 — Micah's own personal lament, likening the moral state of his people to a harvested-out orchard.**
- **Action-type:** lamented (a direct, first-person cry of grief, using an agricultural exhaustion metaphor).
- **Subject:** Micah, first person, continuing his personal voice already established at Mic 1:8/3:8/6:3-8.
- **Operation:** a state — a stated, vivid grief: searching for good fruit (a righteous person) and finding the moral landscape stripped bare, like an orchard after harvest and gleaning.
- **Source:** self — Micah's own grief, explicit.
- **Target:** n/a directly — reflexive lament; the object of his search (moral "fruit") named as absent.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: Micah — given directly stated personal grief, continuing his own established first-person voice from earlier chapters.
- Q3: Stated explicitly.
- Q4: Source = Micah himself, self, explicit.
- Q5: N/A directly — reflexive.
- Q6: State (lament, searching).
- Q7: **Direct linkage to Mic 1:8** — Micah's own first personal lament ("I will lament and wail") recurs here in the book's final chapter, bracketing the whole book with his own voice.
- Q8: N/A — Micah as an individual.
- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: lamented.

**Decision.** Retain — the book's closing chapter opens, as its earlier turning points did, with Micah's own direct personal voice.

### Mic 7:2

> The godly has perished from the earth, and there is no one upright among mankind; they all lie in wait for blood, and each hunts the other with a net.

**Observation.** "The godly [H2623] has perished [H0006] from the earth [H0776G], and there is no [H0369] one upright [H3477G] among mankind [H0120G]; they all [H3605] lie in wait [H0693] for blood [H1818], and each [H0376I] hunts [H6679A] the other [H0251I] with a net [H2764B]."

**Operation 1 — total societal breakdown: no righteous person remains, and predatory violence has become universal.**
- **Action-type:** perished/hunted (a stated total absence of goodness, paired with active, universal predation).
- **Subject:** "the godly" (stated as extinct); "mankind" (given no upright member); "each," hunting "the other" — a totalizing image of mutual predation.
- **Operation:** a state — total moral absence; a movement — active, deliberate hunting of one's own fellow ("brother," H0251I, the same kinship-term used at Obadiah for Edom/Jacob's own violated brotherhood) with a net.
- **Source:** self — each hunter's own predatory choice, explicit.
- **Target:** "the other" — one's own fellow/brother, hunted.

**Interrogative — questions considered.**
- Q1/Q2: "Mankind" — given a total, stated absence of righteousness; "each" — given a directly stated predatory act against "the other," using the kinship term "brother."
- Q3: Stated explicitly.
- Q4: Source = each hunter's own choice, self, explicit.
- Q5: Target = one's own "brother" — kinship betrayal, not merely stranger-on-stranger violence.

- Q9: Sufficient for what is stated.
- Q11: perished (godliness); hunted (predation).

**Decision.** Retain — a further, distinct image (hunting/net) for the book's sustained charge of predatory violence within the community.

- **Subject:** Micah, first person, continuing; the LORD, both the source of the "indignation" being borne and the eventual advocate ("pleads my cause," the identical legal term already used for the LORD's own case AGAINST the people at Mic 6:2, here reversed — the LORD as advocate FOR the confessing individual).

## Passage-level linkages (Q7)

1. **Micah's own voice, bracketing the book**: Mic 1:8 (his first personal lament) → Mic 3:8 (his emphatic self-declaration, "as for me") → Mic 6:3-8 (his own dialogue-voice) → Mic 7:1 (lament) → Mic 7:7 (the identical "as for me" construction, now for personal trust) → Mic 7:9 (his own genuine confession) — Micah's own first-person presence structures the whole book's major turns, closing here at its most personal and resolved.
2. **"My people against itself," reaching its limit**: Mic 2:8 (rising up as enemy against strangers) → Mic 7:5-6 (betrayal within the household itself, "a man's enemies are the men of his own house") — the book's darkest social-collapse thread, closing at its most intimate possible point.
3. **The three-office corruption charge, closing**: Mic 3:1, 9, 11 → Mic 6:11-12 → Mic 7:3 — the identical charge (heads/judges/notables, bribery) recurring a final time, now with explicit "weaving together" collaborative language.
4. **The exodus recital, transformed**: Mic 6:4 (past fact, legal evidence in the LORD's own case) → Mic 7:15 (identical historical reference, now a FUTURE promise of a new exodus) — the same historical anchor serving two opposite rhetorical functions.
5. **The nations, from hostility to total reversal**: Mic 4:11 (hostile gathering, "let our eyes gaze upon Zion") → Mic 7:16-17 (total shame, silence, deafness, dread, "lick the dust like a serpent") — the book's most complete single-collective reversal.
6. **The shepherd-vocabulary thread, three modes**: Mic 2:12 (declared future gathering) → Mic 5:4 (the ruler's own declared shepherding) → Mic 7:14 (a direct petition, asking the LORD to shepherd) — one image, three grammatical postures (future declaration, third-person description, first-person prayer).
7. **"Steadfast love" (chesed, H2617A), the book's closing keyword**: Mic 6:8 (the human requirement, "love kindness") → Mic 7:18 (the LORD's own defining character) → Mic 7:20 (the covenant's own fulfillment, "steadfast love to Abraham") — one word, three positions, carrying the book's ethical argument from requirement to divine ground to promised fulfillment.
8. **"From of old"/"ancient days" bracketing the book's hope**: Mic 5:2 (the coming ruler's own ancient origin) → Mic 7:20 (the covenant sworn "from the days of old") — the same phrase grounding both the messianic hope and the closing covenant appeal.
9. **"Pleads my cause" (rib, H7378/H7379) reversed**: Mic 6:1-2 (the LORD's own legal case AGAINST the people) → Mic 7:9 (the LORD pleading Micah's OWN cause) — the identical legal vocabulary, its direction of advocacy completely reversed.

## Insufficiencies register

- The identity of "they" who come "to you" from every direction (v12) — Israel's own returning exiles, or the converging nations of Mic 4:1-2 — is not disambiguated by this base extract.
- The precise relationship between v12's universal ingathering and v13's continued judgment on "the earth" is not clarified by this base extract's own data.
- The specific content of the promised "marvelous things" (v15) is not detailed.
- Whether "Micah" as a name carries the traditional "who is like Yah(weh)" resonance with v18's own opening question is NOT confirmed by this chapter's own lexicon data (nor by Mic 1:1's), and is named here only as a traditional observation, not asserted as textually established by this base extract.

## Emergent questions log (filed against this passage — not merged across passages; resolved, if at all, at the whole-book read)

- **EQ1.** The "steadfast love" (chesed) thread (Mic 6:8 → 7:18 → 7:20) is one of the cleanest single-keyword arguments found across this study's reading of Micah — worth a dedicated synthesis at the whole-book read, and worth comparing against how chesed functions across the wider prophetic corpus once more books are read.
- **EQ2.** The family-breakdown escalation (Mic 2:8 → 7:5-6) raises a question already flagged at Mic 2 (EQ1 there): how far the "my people" label's own instability (spanning victim, aggressor, and now the household's own internal betrayal) is a deliberate structural device across the whole book — ripe for full treatment at the whole-book read.
- **EQ3.** The exodus recital's transformation (Mic 6:4, past/accusatory → Mic 7:15, future/promissory) is a clean example of the same historical datum serving opposite rhetorical purposes within one book — worth watching for whether this pattern (a fact re-purposed across a book's own argument) recurs elsewhere in the corpus.
- **EQ4.** This is Micah's FINAL chapter — the whole-book read (`report.whole_book_read`) is now the natural next step, gathering every passage's own Emergent-questions and Passage-level-linkages sections across all 7 chapters.
